Nigerian singer, Habeeb Okikiola, popularly known as Portable, has claimed that he received N100m after participating in campaign activities for the All Progressives Congress. The street-pop singer made the claim in a video circulating on social media on Friday. In the video, Portable wore an APC-branded shirt and a cap bearing the inscription of Solomon Adeola, popularly known as Yayi. He also displayed campaign materials featuring the politician. Portable claimed that he woke up to find N100m credited to his account, alleging that the money was sent on the politician’s instructions in recognition of his campaign activities. He said, “My dearest fans! I just woke up to an alert of N100m from Yayi! IBD Dende, oga mi! God bless you. Thank you! Yayi instructed them to send me the money. I took a nap, and God saved me from death. “When I woke up today, I remembered that IBD had asked me to go home yesterday and said he would reach out to me. But some of my senior street brothers and street politicians came to tell me that Yayi was looking for me. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources “Are you the one to tell me that Yayi is looking for me?’ I asked. They wanted to scam me, just as they did when Yayi sent money previously. I did not get a dime then.” He thanked God and the politician for the alleged payment. “Thank you, Lord! Yayi has sent N100m. Thank you, IBD Dende. May your children be glorious! May you live long, my daddy. It shall be well with you. N100m is not a small amount at all!” he said. Tompolo, Zamfara gov mobilise support for Tinubu 2027: Tinubu vows tough action against political violence Kaduna senator rallies support for Tinubu The latest claim comes weeks after the singer publicly acknowledged receiving money for participating in APC campaign activities in support of President Bola Tinubu ahead of the 2027 general elections. In October, Portable had also called on Tinubu and his son, Seyi Tinubu, to give him additional money after performing at an APC rally held at Onikan Stadium in Lagos on October 13. In a video recorded after the rally, the singer was seen lying on the stadium floor, complaining about the physical strain of entertaining supporters and demanding to meet the President and his son. “I want to see Tinubu and Seyi Tinubu; they have almost squeezed me to death. I have fainted; it is Tinubu that is winning. Did we not collect money? Tinubu, pay me more money; I am feeling so much heat,” he said. Portable also acknowledged receiving payment for his participation but insisted that his efforts deserved additional compensation. In another video that circulated earlier in October, the singer said the money he received from campaign activities had improved his financial situation after a period of financial difficulties. However, his latest claim of receiving N100m has not been independently verified, while details of the alleged payment, including its source and purpose, remain unclear.
